title: the Kuiper Line Rising
premise: Cyrus Dravenmoor, the last human technician aboard the automated relay station Kuiper Line, has spent eleven years falsifying 'all systems nominal' reports to hide the extinction of the Meridian colony from two rival fleets hovering on the edge of war over its territory. When the colony's surviving children—cryo-raised and forgotten in a buried habitat—begin sharing a single dream that leads them to his station, Cyrus must decide whether to keep his life-sustaining lie intact or expose the truth. As a fleet tribunal closes in, the children's shared dream proves to be a distress beacon their parents encoded into their sleep, and Cyrus realizes the colony's death was no accident but a corporate purge. In the end, Cyrus sacrifices his anonymity and nearly his life to broadcast the evidence, the children testify as living witnesses, and justice arrives not through either fleet's law but through the truth itself—leaving Cyrus, stripped of his false identity, finally honest about who he is.
about_author: Odile Villalobos is a former radio astronomer who spent three winters at a remote Andean observatory, an experience that shapes her fiction's obsession with isolation and signals from the dark. She writes science fiction that treats silence as a character and survival as a moral question.

chapters.title: All Systems Nominal
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. On relay station Kuiper Line, Cyrus records his 4,017th false status report while tending the automated arrays that once served the thriving Meridian colony below. His routines are rituals of grief: logging weather for no one, maintaining equipment for ghosts. The chapter establishes his guilt and the lie he lives inside. Emotional beat: hollow devotion—the comfort and rot of a lie kept too long.

chapters.title: The Children Under the Ice
chapters.summary: POV: alternating between Cyrus and Nia, eldest of seven cryo-raised children in the buried habitat. Nia keeps the younger ones alive on failing rations, telling them rescue is coming because she cannot bear the alternative. A seismic tremor cracks the habitat's seal, forcing her toward the surface—and toward the station's signal. Emotional beat: fierce, exhausted hope masquerading as certainty.

chapters.title: Signal in the Snow
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. The station detects movement it was never designed to detect: small heat signatures crossing the ice. Cyrus watches them approach on cameras meant for maintenance drones, paralyzed by the impossible arithmetic of mouths he cannot feed. When they reach the airlock, he opens it before he decides to. Emotional beat: terror cracking open into reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: The Same Dream
chapters.summary: POV: Nia. The children reveal they all dream identically—a corridor of blue light, a voice counting down—which Nia hid for months, fearing madness. Cyrus recognizes the pattern as encoded data embedded in the colony's cryo-systems. Someone programmed the children's sleep. Emotional beat: uncanny dread giving way to the first real clue that the colony's death had authors.

chapters.title: Two Fleets at the Edge
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Through intercepted fleet traffic, we learn the Concord and the Vellamore armada both believe Meridian alive, each deterred by Cyrus's fake reports claiming the colony is armed and neutral. His lie is the only peace treaty in existence. Now the children's presence risks everything if detected. Emotional beat: vertigo—the weight of being the sole pillar holding back a war.

chapters.title: What the Logs Buried
chapters.summary: POV: Nia. Decoding the dream-data with Cyrus, they excavate the station's sealed archives and find the purge order: the colony was terminated deliberately by the Halcyon Combine to trigger a territorial claim clause. The children's parents knew and hid the evidence in their own children's minds. Emotional beat: grief transmuting into purpose; mourning becomes testimony.

chapters.title: The Tribunal Arrives Early
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. A joint Concord-Vellamore inspection vessel jumps into range weeks ahead of schedule, summoned by an anomalous energy reading from the children's decoding work. Cyrus has seventy-two hours to erase seven children from a station built to be transparent. Emotional beat: claustrophobic countdown; every choice now costs someone something.

chapters.title: A Lie Held by Seven Hands
chapters.summary: POV: Nia. The children rehearse playing station orphans of a different dead colony while Cyrus fabricates a cover identity for them. But the youngest, Tam, breaks under questioning during a remote interview, nearly exposing them. Nia realizes they cannot live inside someone else's lie—they can only survive by telling their own truth. Emotional beat: the breaking point of deception as protection.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. With the tribunal boarding, Cyrus hijacks the station's full array and transmits the purge evidence, the dream-code, and his eleven years of falsified logs—confessing his own crime alongside the Combine's. Boarders storm the transmitter room as the signal spreads to both fleets. He is shot protecting the children and left bleeding beneath the console still streaming truth. Emotional beat: cathartic self-destruction; the lie dies so the truth can breathe.

chapters.title: The Counting Voice
chapters.summary: POV: Nia, then Cyrus briefly. Both fleets halt, convened by shared outrage rather than treaty; the Combine's officers are arrested by their own allies. The dream's final count completes—it was never a warning but a promise: 'seven voices will finish what we started.' Cyrus survives, tried outside any fleet's jurisdiction and sentenced to serve the children's new settlement. Invisible no longer, he begins recording true reports—for people who are listening. Emotional beat: quiet, earned restoration; identity rebuilt on honesty instead of hiding.
